clue.text: Speed up for ages, then stop calamitously

indicators.note: doing something calamitously means making a wreck of it, so the words before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the twelve letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A driver who has been dawdling for ages accelerates and then has to brake disastrously.
explanation.definitionFit: To press the accelerator pedal of a car is an informal idiom for going faster or hurrying.

clue.text: Messages sent by Lawrence to poor Mrs Gale

indicators.note: the woman is in poor shape, so her title and surname are knocked out of order

blocks.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, by his initials
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia sends letters to some unfortunate lady called Mrs Gale.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence is the famous T. E. Lawrence, so only his initials are used.
explanation.definitionFit: These were written communications transmitted by wire and delivered on paper, the classic form of urgent message.

clue.text: Turn over page on lake

indicators.note: in a down entry, one item sitting on another means it is placed above, so it comes first

blocks.note: p is the standard abbreviation for page
lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: Someone flips a page of a book about a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A lough is an Irish lake, like the Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers break and invert the soil of a field with a blade, so the verb means to turn earth over.

clue.text: One not included when it's lighting-up time?

definitions.text: One not included when it's lighting-up time?

blocks.clueFragment: One not included when it's lighting-up time?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone left out at lighting-up time, the hour when vehicles must switch on their lamps
setter's reading: the moment people light cigarettes, which one person declines to join

explanation.walkthrough: Lighting-up time is the legal hour for car lights in Britain; here it means lighting a cigarette, which excludes someone who never does.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who does not use tobacco would naturally sit out when everyone else lights a cigarette.

clue.text: See 1 across
Point of growing things, some with ornate leaves

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run inside the words
read as the verb, the words leave behind or give out a run of letters within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A description of plants, some of them bearing decorative foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like plant foliage, which suits the garden picture, but it works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp prickle on a rose or bramble stem is the pointed part of such a plant.

clue.text: Hospital department I depend on without reservation

blocks.note: ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
taken as written
to depend on is to rely

explanation.surface: A patient admits total dependence on one hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with no holding back means doing it completely and wholly, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Biblical character and motoring organisation man

blocks.note: the Automobile Association, a British breakdown and motoring club
a man's name, short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A figure from scripture paired with a breakdown-service patrolman.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, a British roadside rescue club.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder brother of Moses and first high priest of the Israelites appears in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Blessing everyone coming in is swell

indicators.note: something coming in enters another word and sits inside it

blocks.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A good thing that includes everybody is said to be just great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like the slang adjective for excellent, but it is the verb meaning to expand.
explanation.definitionFit: To puff up and grow larger, as a sail or a belly does, is a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Complain to leading restaurateur in Bruges about fast food

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun; the definition is a mass noun

indicators.note: the leading part of a word is its opening letter only
about means moved around, so the Belgian city's name gets scrambled with its addition

blocks.note: to beef is slang for to grumble
opening letter of this word
the Belgian city, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests to a top restaurant owner in Bruges about the junk food served.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes in among the city's letters, and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamburgers made of minced beef are the staple of quick-service takeaway chains.

clue.text: Against a trio performing in Canada?

definitions.note: describes where the answer is rather than naming it, hence the question mark

indicators.note: performing suggests the musicians moving into new positions on stage

blocks.note: leaning against something is leaning on it
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a group of three musicians playing a gig in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large province of central Canada, home to Toronto and Ottawa, so it lies within that country.

clue.text: Passionately evil bosses reformed before end of play

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the bosses' description is reshaped
the end of a word is its final letter
one part placed before another is written first

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Wicked managers mend their ways with great fervour, before the end of the drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with fixated, all-consuming intensity is close in sense to acting with ardent feeling.

clue.text: People promised to give these battle calls

blocks.note: an engagement is a military clash
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what betrothed people hand over, with talk of fighting and shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promised' is the old sense of betrothed, so the people are fiancés.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple pledged to marry traditionally mark it with a jewelled band given to the bride-to-be.

clue.text: Supporter to get ¿1,000 a game

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
a grand, a thousand, is G in slang

explanation.surface: A sports fan is paid a thousand pounds for a single match.
explanation.walkthrough: G for grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars. Brag is an old British card game, a forerunner of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a three-card gambling game played in Britain, closely related to poker.

clue.text: Mean people hide cigarette-lighter components

blocks.note: an animal's hide is its skin
a lighter strikes sparks from a small stone

explanation.surface: Stingy folk conceal the working parts of their lighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb to conceal, but it is the noun for an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Misers who hate parting with money are proverbially tight-fisted, the noun for such stingy individuals.

clue.text: One with no wheels, still to be tested?

definitions.text: One with no wheels, still to be tested?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone without a car of their own
setter's reading: a person who has not yet passed a road examination and so may not take the wheel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' is slang for a car, and the test is the driving test.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has no licence and does not operate a car is described by this hyphenated noun.

clue.text: New word for men standing around igloos, drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and out of order, so the snow houses' letters are muddled
in a down entry, standing means set upright, read from bottom to top
around means surrounding, with one part placed either side of the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Tipsy men gather around their snow houses, needing a term for the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshly coined term or expression newly brought into a language is the technical name for this.

clue.text: Person that is holding dog having paws seen to?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for the treatment; the definition describes undergoing it

indicators.note: something holding another item has it inside its grip

blocks.note: a man is a person
i.e., Latin id est, means that is
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone holds a dog while its feet are attended to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paws' is jocular for hands, and the dog in the surface makes it sound literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic treatment of the hands and fingernails is what having one's 'paws' looked after humorously means.

clue.text: Cafe with calm atmosphere won't take 50% off

indicators.note: taking fifty per cent off removes half the letters of the word

blocks.note: rest is calm, repose
an aura is a distinctive atmosphere
the word without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A tranquil eatery refuses to offer a half-price discount.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of the four-letter word goes, leaving its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are establishments serving meals to paying customers, so one stands loosely for the other.

clue.text: Places in Oslo citizens avoid

indicators.note: in means the letters are found within the next words
the outer letters of the two words are avoided, leaving only a stretch in the middle

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Certain spots in the Norwegian capital that residents steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural of locus, a site or position, used in maths and genetics for locations.

clue.text: Sneers, which irritates woman standing on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing means set upright, read from bottom to top
in a down entry, on top means placed first

blocks.note: Ms is the title for a woman
irks means annoys

explanation.surface: A woman stands over someone, smirking in a way that annoys them.
explanation.definitionFit: A smug, self-satisfied smile is close to a scornful curl of the lip, both being contemptuous expressions.

clue.text: Taking flat in Gateshead with prudish girl is a bloomer!

blocks.note: flat means level or even
taken as written
the place name splits as Gates-head, telling you to take only the head, its first letter
prim means prudish
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Renting a flat in Gateshead with a strait-laced young woman is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town on Tyne opposite Newcastle; only its 'head' letter is used. A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that bears flowers can jokingly be called a bloomer, and this yellow-flowered plant opens in the evening.

clue.text: Craft is back underneath once more

indicators.note: going back means read in the opposite direction, up the column
in a down entry, a piece underneath another comes after it

blocks.note: ex means former, once
art is craft or skill

explanation.surface: A craft comes back once more, as though revived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once more' looks like a single phrase meaning again, but it splits: 'once' is wordplay and 'more' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional, beyond the usual amount, is more of it.

clue.text: Little prayer when backing vehicle in, say

indicators.note: in means placed inside another piece
backing means moving in reverse, so the combination is read the other way

blocks.note: e.g., for example, is short for say
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A quick prayer said while reversing a car into a space, say.
explanation.walkthrough: The vehicle goes inside the abbreviation for 'say', and then the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A short blessing said before a meal, giving thanks for the food, is a brief prayer.

clue.text: Fruit from South Africa - a must - is coming back

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so these words are read right to left

blocks.note: the abbreviation for South Africa
taken as written

explanation.surface: Imported fruit from South Africa is an essential purchase and is returning to the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose-skinned citrus fruit like a mandarin, originally from Japan, is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Change suit, union leader having gone inside university

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, which is the one lost here
something having gone has been taken away
inside means placed within another word

blocks.note: to vary is to change
taken as written
its first letter is the one to remove

explanation.surface: A trade union chief changes into a smart suit to visit a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Varsity is a dated British word for university, used especially for Oxford–Cambridge sports fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal shortening of the word, mainly used of sports teams and rivalries between colleges.

clue.text: Soldiers accept bill for floral arrangement

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a/c, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Troops agree to pay the invoice for a flower display.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's corps of electrical and mechanical engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically, it is a flower cluster with stalked blossoms set along a central stem, a natural arrangement of flowers.

clue.text: Suppose piano must be removed and carry on

indicators.note: something that must be removed is taken out of the word

blocks.note: to presume is to suppose
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a piano has to be shifted before work can continue.
explanation.definitionFit: To start again after a pause or interruption is to continue.
